source: Cox & D'Antonio 3e Table 6.7, PDF pages 257-258 (printed pp. 200-201)
about: Rendered PDF pages 257 and 258, folios 200 and 201 (running heads "200   Acoustic Absorbers and Diffusers" and "Porous sound absorption   201"). Title as printed on the first page: "Table 6.7 Effective flow resistivity values for ground surfaces and other parameters" ("Table 6.7" italic); the continuation page repeats it as "Table 6.7 (Continued) Effective flow resistivity values for ground surfaces and other parameters". Five columns, headings in italic, repeated identically on both pages: "Surface"; "Effective flow resistivity (rayl m-1)" (the -1 a superscript); "Water content (%)"; "Porosity"; "Porosity decay zeta (m-1)" (the Greek zeta as printed). Seven bold group headings run down the Surface column: Snow, Forests and crops, Grass, Earth (first page), then Rock, Other, Sand (second page); the Earth group is split across the page break and its heading is NOT repeated on the continuation page, so the first rows of folio 201 (Arable, Cultivated soil, Wet and compacted soil, Heath) are carried under group Earth. Each heading is recorded as the group field on its rows and is not itself a row. 63 rows, in page order. Units: the printed unit rayl m-1 is the library unit Pa s/m2, so every flow resistivity is carried over with factor 1; the powers of ten are expanded ("1 × 10^4–3 × 10^4" becomes ranges [10000.0, 30000.0], "(540 ± 92) × 10^3" becomes 540000.0 with uncertainty 92000.0, "≈3 × 10^7" becomes 30000000.0 flagged approximate). Cell conventions on the page: an en-dashed interval is a range; "−76 to 47" and "−400 to 80" are ranges with a negative low end; a dash "-" is an empty cell, and so is a blank cell (both kinds occur, apparently at random, and both mean the quantity is absent from the row; each row's note says which it was). Footnote markers [a], [b] and [c] are printed in square brackets beside individual cells; the footnotes, verbatim, are "a Fitted using Delany and Bazley model.", "b Fitted using semi-phenomenological model." and "c Fitted using variable porosity model." Seven surfaces (Sports field, Lawn, Long grass, Pasture, Bare earth, Arable, Urban, and Heath with a defect noted below) print THREE flow resistivity lines under one name, one per fit; each becomes its own row with variant set to the footnote text as printed. For those surfaces the water content, porosity and porosity decay cells are printed ONCE, typographically on the line of the first fit, and they are recorded on that first row only, with a note on the other two pointing back to it; where such a porosity cell itself carries a marker (always [b] in this table, e.g. "0.34–1 [b]"), the marker text is quoted in that row's note rather than being made into a separate row. Two sand surfaces (Coarse sand, pore size 98 μm and Fine sand, pore size 65 um) print FOUR lines each, one per water content, and become four rows with variant "water content 0 %" and so on, the water content also going to its own field. Grassland prints two unmarked ranges on two lines with nothing to pair them with, so both go to reported. Printed defects, transcribed and not repaired: the first Heath line prints its low end as "1.7.3 × 10^5", with two decimal points, which is not a readable number (the cell is therefore unquantified), and that same line is marked [b] rather than [a], so Heath prints two [b] lines and no [a]. Oddity in the Porosity column: six rows (Mineral layer beneath mixed deciduous forest 36.5, Humus on pine forest floor 58.1, Pine forest litter 38.9, Grass root layer in loamy sand 48 ± 4, Loamy sand 37.5, Bare sandy plain 26.9) print values far above 1 in a column that everywhere else prints fractions; they are plainly percentages on the page, and each is held as printed in porosity_percent (with the ± 4 of the grass root layer in its uncertainty) rather than in porosity, which holds a fraction; the column's missing unit is registered in docs/ERRATA.md. What the prose says: on folio 199 (PDF 256), "The ground is often modelled as a porous absorber. The Delany and Bazley formulations have been used quite extensively to obtain the characteristic impedance and wavenumber, even though these equations were developed for use with glass fibre rather than loose granular materials. For this, flow resistivity values for typical ground surfaces are needed, and Table 6.7 gives the appropriate values. While the Delany and Bazley model" - continuing on folio 202 (PDF 259) - "works reasonably well above about 250 Hz, at lower frequencies, the characteristic impedance and wavenumber have significant errors, resulting in inaccurate predictions of excess attenuations. Modelling the porosity to vary with depth (see Section 6.6.3) or using a semi-phenomenological model (see Section 6.5.3) is usually more accurate." On folio 214 (PDF 271) the book defines what "effective" means, after Equation 6.45, sigma_e ≈ 4 s_p^2 sigma / phi: "where sigma is the flow resistivity and s_p is a characteristic length, which can be taken to be 0.5 in many cases, meaning the effective flow resistivity is just the flow resistivity scaled by the porosity", and what the last column is: "The change in soil properties is modelled as an exponential decrease in porosity with depth. The rate of change in porosity with depth is given by zeta, and some values for this parameter are given in Table 6.7." Credit: the table carries no per-row superscripts into the chapter 6 reference list; instead a "Sources:" block under the continuation page credits the whole table, printed verbatim as "Sources: Horoshenkov, K.V., Mohamed, M.H.A., J. Acoust. Soc. Am., 120, 1910–1921, 2006; Attenborough, L., Bashir, I., Taherzadeh, S., J. Acoust. Soc. Am., 129, 2806–2819, 2011; Attenborough, K., J. Acoust. Soc. Am., 81, 93–102, 1982; Attenborough, K., Acta Acust., 1, 213–226, 1993; Berryman, J.G., Appl. Phys. Lett., 37, 382–384, 1980; Embleton, T.F.W., Piercy, J.E., Daigle, G.A., J. Acoust. Soc. Am., 74, 1239–1244, 1983; Martens, M.J.M., van der Haijden, L.A.M., Walthaus, H.H.J., van Rens, W.J.J., J. Acoust. Soc. Am., 78, 970–980, 1985; Datt, P., Kapil, J.C., Kumar, A., Srivastava, P.K., Appl. Acoust., 101, 15–23, 2016." All eight are resolved into attributed_to under the key "table" on every row. Note that the 2011 entry is printed "Attenborough, L." where the other two Attenborough entries are "Attenborough, K."; the initial is transcribed as printed here and only the surname is used in attributed_to. Nothing on the page gives a measurement frequency or a measurement method for any row beyond the three fitting models of the footnotes.
